subject: Difference between metadata values of an image and timestamp noted on the image

messages.author: 168f21f5ce6ef78a
messages.subject: Difference between metadata values of an image and timestamp noted on the image
parts:
Hi,

I am currently working on a camera trap dataset and I have extracted all data using the recordTable function. Then I used R to select the snapshot moment every 2 seconds. But when I checked the images that were selected as snapshot moments (so where time finishes by an even number), I noticed that the metadata extracted by Exiftool and camtrapR for the time was sometimes slightly different from the timestamp written directly on the image. Here is an example to make things clearer. 

Image 03080345.JPG

Timestamp noted on the image : 09:26:53
Timestamp extracted usding Exiftool and CamtrapR (record table): 09:26:54

There therefore seems to be a difference a 1 second (sometimes no difference, less frequently a difference of 2 seconds) between the metadata of the image and the timestamp on the image. It appears that the metadata corresponding to the date and time is slightly different, maybe because it corresponds to the time the file was created.

I am trying to see if it is an error on my side or if it already happened to other people, and also if it will have an impact if I am working on metadata values (and not timestamp on the image) to extract snapshop moment.

Thank you for you help and don't hesitate if you would like more information or to see my data.

Best regards,

Emeline Auda

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Difference between metadata values of an image and timestamp noted on the image
parts:
Hi Emeline,

thank you, this is interesting and I haven't seen this before.

I suspect there is some sort of delay during image processing in the camera, which leads to the time difference. Maybe the camera system queries the internal time twice: once when writing the data field in the image, and again later when writing the EXIF metadata. That would be beyond my control, but it's just speculation.

There's not a lot we can do here. Personally I'd just go with the metadata, since they are easy to read out without error. Even if they are a second late. For very time-critical applications a different camera model might be more suitable though.

The alternative would be to use optical character recognition to extract the time from the data field in the images, but that is not very reliable unfortunately and may misread the numbers and requires checking. See ?OCRdataFields.

Best regards,

Jürgen
